subject: en_read
source: English National Curriculum — English programmes of study: key stages 1 and 2 (lower KS2, Year 4), DfE 2013 — reading comprehension

weeks.topic: Skimming and scanning — 'The Lion, the Witch and the Wardrobe' (C. S. Lewis)
objectives: Skim a chapter for the gist
Scan for key words and details

weeks.topic: Inference: character motives — Edmund in Narnia
objectives: Infer why a character behaves as he does
Support inferences with quotations

weeks.topic: Settings and atmosphere: the winter world of Narnia
objectives: Explain how vocabulary creates atmosphere
Compare the wardrobe world with the real world

weeks.topic: Historical fiction: stories set in Ancient Egypt
objectives: Identify historical details in a story
Discuss how the setting affects events

weeks.topic: Information texts on Ancient Egypt: note-taking
objectives: Take notes from an information text
Organise notes under headings

weeks.topic: Myths: Egyptian and Norse creation stories
objectives: Compare creation myths from two cultures
Identify the role of gods and goddesses

weeks.topic: Narrative poetry — 'The Pied Piper of Hamelin' (Robert Browning)
objectives: Retell the story told in the poem
Discuss how rhyme and rhythm carry the story

weeks.topic: Explanation texts: the human body
objectives: Identify the structure of an explanation text
Retrieve information from text and diagrams

weeks.topic: Prediction with evidence — 'Varjak Paw' (S. F. Said)
objectives: Predict events using details stated and implied
Review predictions as the story develops

weeks.topic: Word choice and vocabulary — 'Varjak Paw'
objectives: Explore how word choice creates meaning
Use a thesaurus to compare synonyms

weeks.topic: Summarising main ideas across paragraphs
objectives: Identify the main idea of each paragraph
Write a summary of a whole article

weeks.topic: Playscripts: comparing a story and its play version
objectives: Compare a story with its playscript version
Discuss what changes in a script

weeks.topic: Kennings and Anglo-Saxon riddles
objectives: Solve riddles and kennings
Explain how compound words create images

weeks.topic: Fact, opinion and bias in news reports
objectives: Distinguish fact, opinion and bias
Discuss how headlines influence readers

weeks.topic: Review: inference, summary and vocabulary
objectives: Practise comprehension questions on an unseen text
Revise skimming, scanning and summarising

weeks.topic: Explorers' journals and biographies
objectives: Retrieve dates and places from explorers' journals
Sequence events in an explorer's life

weeks.topic: Relationships in adventure fiction — 'Kensuke's Kingdom' (Michael Morpurgo)
objectives: Infer how a relationship changes over time
Use evidence from several chapters

weeks.topic: Author's craft: setting and survival — 'Kensuke's Kingdom'
objectives: Explain how the island setting shapes the story
Identify how the author builds tension

weeks.topic: Persuasive texts: travel brochures
objectives: Identify persuasive techniques in brochures
Evaluate how convincing a brochure is

weeks.topic: Empathy and viewpoint — 'Bill's New Frock' (Anne Fine)
objectives: Discuss how the main character feels and why
Consider the story from different viewpoints

weeks.topic: Figurative language in poetry: similes and metaphors
objectives: Identify similes and metaphors in poems
Explain the images they create

weeks.topic: Discussion texts: balanced arguments
objectives: Identify arguments for and against
Decide which argument is stronger and why

weeks.topic: Stories from other cultures — 'The Firework-Maker's Daughter' (Philip Pullman)
objectives: Identify cultural details in the setting
Discuss the main character's quest and courage

weeks.topic: Comparing characters within and across texts
objectives: Compare two characters using evidence
Explain similarities and differences

weeks.topic: Biographies of people who made a difference
objectives: Retrieve key achievements from a biography
Discuss why a person is significant

weeks.topic: Perspective and scale — 'The Borrowers' (Mary Norton)
objectives: Explain how the author shows the world from a tiny viewpoint
Infer how the Borrowers feel about humans

weeks.topic: Reading comprehension assessment: Terms 1 and 2
objectives: Answer retrieval, vocabulary, inference and summary questions
Explain answers with evidence

weeks.topic: Character description — 'Charlie and the Chocolate Factory' (Roald Dahl)
objectives: Infer characters' personalities from descriptions
Explain how the author makes characters memorable

weeks.topic: Flowcharts and explanations: from cocoa bean to chocolate bar
objectives: Follow a process shown in a flowchart
Retrieve information from text and images

weeks.topic: Free verse and performance poetry
objectives: Discuss how free verse differs from rhyming poetry
Prepare a poem for performance

weeks.topic: Humour and unreliable narrators — 'The Diary of a Killer Cat' (Anne Fine)
objectives: Explain how the narrator's voice creates humour
Infer what really happened

weeks.topic: Compare and contrast: life in different places
objectives: Compare information about two places from different texts
Organise similarities and differences in a table

weeks.topic: Legends from around the world
objectives: Compare legends from different countries
Identify common features of legends

weeks.topic: Book reviews: justifying opinions
objectives: Write and discuss reviews of books read
Justify opinions with reasons and examples

weeks.topic: Independent reading and reading journals
objectives: Choose a book independently and keep a reading journal
Reflect on the themes of the book

weeks.topic: End-of-year reading assessment: Year 4
objectives: Answer comprehension questions on fiction, non-fiction and poetry
Use evidence to support answers

weeks.topic: Review and summer reading plan
objectives: Reflect on reading progress
Plan a summer reading list
